  "summary": "Fixes an aliasing bug in MuHash3072::operator/= when an object divides itself. By caching the divisor's numerator before multiplying the dividend's numerator, it prevents reading the modified numerator when the divisor is *this. Unit and fuzz tests are updated to cover self-division where the denominator is not 1.",
  "problem": "When MuHash3072 divides by itself (x /= x), the first step mutates m_numerator before the second step reads div.m_numerator. If the denominator is not 1, this results in an incorrect state (1/D instead of the empty set), though no current node or index logic executes self-division.",

    "PR description: 'When that is the case, the second step reads the numerator that the first step already updated, so x /= x actually leaves 1/D instead of the empty set... No code in the node/index divides MuHash objects by themselves, so runnings nodes are not affected.'"

result.summary: Fixes an aliasing bug in MuHash3072::operator/= when an object divides itself. By caching the divisor's numerator before multiplying the dividend's numerator, it prevents reading the modified numerator when the divisor is *this. Unit and fuzz tests are updated to cover self-division where the denominator is not 1.
result.problem: When MuHash3072 divides by itself (x /= x), the first step mutates m_numerator before the second step reads div.m_numerator. If the denominator is not 1, this results in an incorrect state (1/D instead of the empty set), though no current node or index logic executes self-division.
evidence: PR description: 'When that is the case, the second step reads the numerator that the first step already updated, so x /= x actually leaves 1/D instead of the empty set... No code in the node/index divides MuHash objects by themselves, so runnings nodes are not affected.'
result.card: Fixes a self-aliasing bug in MuHash3072::operator/= where dividing an object by itself mutates the numerator before reading it for the denominator step. If the initial denominator is not 1, self-division leaves an incorrect state rather than the empty set. Running nodes are not impacted because no active index or node code performs self-division on MuHash objects, but the fix hardens the cryptographic library and updates unit and fuzz tests.
